subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which term describes a melody supported by chords moving in the same rhythm?
questions.explain: Homophonic texture is a clear melody accompanied by chords.

questions.q: In vocal technique, 'vibrato' is:
options: A slight, regular wavering of pitch to enrich the tone
questions.explain: Vibrato is a slight, regular variation in pitch that adds warmth to a sustained note.

questions.q: Which structure follows the pattern ABA?
questions.explain: Ternary form has three sections in an ABA pattern, where the A material returns.

questions.q: Which Italian tempo term means 'fast and lively'?
questions.explain: Allegro means fast and lively, whereas adagio and largo are slow.

questions.q: Which time signature is an example of compound time?
questions.explain: 6/8 is compound time because each beat divides into three quavers (two dotted-crotchet beats).

questions.q: What is the main advantage of using a metronome when practising a performance?
options: It helps you keep a steady, accurate tempo
questions.explain: A metronome sounds a steady beat, helping a performer keep an accurate and consistent tempo.

questions.q: What is the difference between a solo and an ensemble performance?
options: A solo is loud; an ensemble is quiet
A solo is one performer; an ensemble is a group
questions.explain: A solo is performed by one player, while an ensemble involves a group performing together.

questions.q: 'Sight-reading' means:
options: Playing music you have not seen before, at first sight
questions.explain: Sight-reading is performing a piece of music you are seeing for the first time.

questions.q: 'Transposition' means:
options: Moving music up or down to a different pitch or key
Changing the dynamics of a piece
questions.explain: Transposition moves a piece of music to a higher or lower pitch (a different key).

questions.q: A sharp sign in front of a note does what?
options: Lowers the pitch by a semitone
Raises the pitch by a semitone
questions.explain: A sharp raises a note's pitch by one semitone.

questions.q: When sequencing in a DAW, individual notes are often arranged on a:
questions.explain: In a DAW, notes are commonly entered and arranged on a piano roll along a track timeline.

questions.q: How many different pitches does a pentatonic scale contain?
questions.explain: A pentatonic scale is made up of five different pitches per octave.

questions.q: What does a single dot placed after a note do to its value?
options: Adds half the note's value again
questions.explain: A dot after a note increases its length by half of its original value.

questions.q: The interval of an octave between two notes of the same letter name spans how many semitones?
questions.explain: An octave spans twelve semitones from one note to the next of the same name.

questions.q: A texture described as 'monophonic' has:
options: A single melodic line with no accompaniment
questions.explain: Monophonic texture is a single unaccompanied melodic line.

questions.q: In music technology, 'panning' a sound controls:
options: Its position between the left and right speakers
questions.explain: Panning places a sound in the stereo field, between the left and right speakers.

questions.q: On a string instrument, the technique 'pizzicato' means to:
options: Pluck the strings with the finger
questions.explain: Pizzicato instructs the player to pluck the strings rather than bow them.

questions.q: 'Composing to a brief' means:
options: Composing music to meet a given set of requirements or purpose
questions.explain: Composing to a brief means writing music that fulfils a specified purpose or set of instructions.

questions.q: The harmonic minor scale differs from the natural minor by raising which note?
questions.explain: The harmonic minor scale raises the seventh note by a semitone, creating a leading note.

questions.q: What does a natural sign do?
options: Raises a note by a tone
Lowers a note by a tone
Cancels a previous sharp or flat
questions.explain: A natural cancels a sharp or flat, returning the note to its natural pitch.

questions.q: In a melody-and-accompaniment texture, the accompaniment:
options: Supports the melody with chords or a bass line
questions.explain: The accompaniment supports the main melody, often with chords or a bass line.

questions.q: On a guitar, a 'capo' is used to:
options: Raise the pitch of all strings to play in a different key
questions.explain: A capo clamps across the fretboard to raise the pitch of every string, changing the key.
